newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says 1997 mini-budget probable.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says 1997 mini-budget probable.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Sunday that Italy was likely to have to pass a mini-budget in 1997 but he would not be sure until official state accounts were published.

"We'll see the data and then decide," Prodi told reporters in the northern city of Bologna. "It is probable that with the situation we are facing that we could or should have recourse to a supplementary budget, but I don't yet have the data to hand."
The state accounts are due to be published in late February or early March.

Prodi was answering questions on comments by Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi at a conference in Milan earlier in which Ciampi said that Italy would act on spending if it decided to pass a mini-budget.

Prodi pushed through a 1997 austerity budget to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($39.3 billion) of this year's deficit in a bid to get Italy in shape for planned Economic and Monetary Union in 1999. But economists say those measures may still not be enough.

Analysts also say that an overshoot in the 1996 public sector borrowing requirement has left a hole in state accounts, meaning the government will have to implement a supplementary budget of up to 25 trillion lire to plug the gap.
Italy ran up a public sector deficit of 138.5 trillion lire last year compared with an original target of 109.4 trillion. ($1=1,588 lire)
